business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (Item 1 Business)
business_model.claim: Visa sells transaction processing over its VisaNet network. This mainly means authorization, clearing and settlement, and it sits between consumers, issuing and acquiring financial institutions and sellers.
quotes: We provide transaction processing services (primarily authorization, clearing and settlement) among consumers, issuing and acquiring financial institutions and sellers

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (Item 1 Business)
business_model.claim: Visa's direct customers are financial institutions, along with sellers, fintechs, digital wallets and governments. It is not a lender: it does not issue cards or bear credit risk on account holders' borrowing. It has over 14,000 financial institution clients.
quotes: Visa is not a financial institution.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (Item 7 revenue components table)
business_model.claim: Net revenue for the latest fiscal year was $45,903 (table in millions). It is built from service revenue of $19,918, data processing revenue of 23,374, international transaction revenue of 15,251 and other revenue of 5,677, less client incentives of (18,317), all in the same table in millions.

Revenue lines follow volume and activity drivers. Payments volume drives service revenue, processed transactions drive data processing revenue, and cross-border volume drives international transaction revenue. Latest-year growth was 10% in nominal payments volume, 9% in processed transactions and 15% in nominal cross-border volume excluding Europe.
quotes: Payments volume is the primary driver for our service revenue, and the number of processed transactions is the primary driver for our data processing revenue.
Service revenue increased in fiscal 2026 over the prior year primarily due to growth in nominal payments volume of 10%, select pricing modifications and growth in card benefits.

business_model.claim: Client incentives are the main contra-revenue cost. They are paid to financial institution clients, sellers and other partners to grow volume and acceptance. They were $18.3 billion, up 16%, and they rise with payments volume.
quotes: Paid to financial institution clients, sellers and other business partners to grow payments volume
Client incentives were $18.3 billion, up 16% over the prior year.

business_model.claim: Value-added services are a fast-growing revenue source. They produced $14.2 billion in the latest fiscal year, up 31%. The largest contributions came from Issuing Solutions and Advisory and Other Services.
quotes: Value-added services revenue in fiscal 2026 increased 31% over the prior year, reflecting growth across all portfolios, with the largest contributions from Issuing Solutions and Advisory and Other Services.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (Item 7 net revenue table)
business_model.claim: Revenue is reported by geography: U.S. net revenue was $17,423 and international net revenue was 28,480 (table in millions). International grew faster, at 17% against 11% for the U.S.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (Item 7 operating expenses)
business_model.claim: Operating expenses were $17,793 (table in millions), up 11%, mainly from higher personnel and marketing costs. Personnel was 7,934 and marketing was 2,315. Marketing rose with FIFA World Cup and Olympic-related client marketing and campaigns, and personnel rose with headcount, compensation and severance.
quotes: Operating expenses increased 11% over the prior year, primarily driven by higher personnel and marketing expenses.

business_model.claim: Litigation provisions are a large and variable cost line, linked to the interchange multidistrict litigation. The provision was 1,764 against 2,562 a year earlier (table in millions). Under the U.S. retrospective responsibility plan, Visa recovers covered losses by lowering class B conversion rates into class A shares.
quotes: Under the U.S. retrospective responsibility plan, we recover the monetary liabilities related to the U.S. covered litigation through a downward adjustment to the rates at which shares of our class B-1, B-2 and B-3 common stock ultimately convert into shares of class A common stock.

business_model.basis: inferred from the income and cash flow statements; the ratio itself is not stated in the items
business_model.claim: The model converts revenue into cash with little capital spending. Operating income was 28,110 and operating cash flow was 23,728, against purchases of property, equipment and technology of (1,671) (tables in millions).

Cash is returned mainly through buybacks and dividends. Visa repurchased 61 million class A shares for $20.5 billion in the latest fiscal year. The board raised the quarterly dividend 16% to $0.780 per share.
quotes: During fiscal 2026, we repurchased 61 million shares of our class A common stock in the open market for $20.5 billion.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (Item 1A Risk Factors)
business_model.claim: Interchange fees are not Visa's revenue, but they affect competitiveness and volume. Regulation of them is a key external risk to the revenue model.
quotes: Although we generally do not receive IRF revenue directly, IRFs are a key competitive factor that affects our overall payments volume and net revenue.

business_model.claim: Client concentration is a stated risk. A significant part of net revenue comes from Visa's largest clients, and clients can generally issue non-Visa products.
quotes: Because a significant portion of our net revenue is concentrated among our largest clients, the loss of business from any one of them could materially harm our business, results of operations and financial condition.

competitive_position.claim: Visa operates at very large scale: it processed 281 billion of the 355 billion Visa-brand transactions in fiscal 2026, and serves over 14,000 financial institutions.
quotes: Of the 355 billion total transactions, 281 billion were processed by Visa.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K income statement and MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Net revenue grew to 45,903 (table in millions) in fiscal 2026 from 40,000 (table in millions), up 15%. Management attributes the growth to cross-border volume, processed transactions and payments volume, partly offset by higher client incentives.
quotes: Net revenue increased 15% over the prior year, primarily due to the growth in nominal cross-border volume, processed transactions and nominal payments volume, partially offset by higher client incentives.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the income statement. The link to the lower litigation provision is inferred from the line items.
competitive_position.claim: Profitability is high. Operating income was 28,110 (table in millions) and net income 23,504 (table in millions) in fiscal 2026, up from 23,994 and 20,058 a year earlier.
Volumes grew across the board. Nominal payments volume rose 10%, processed transactions rose 9%, and nominal cross-border volume rose 15% excluding intra-Europe.
quotes: Nominal payments volume growth of 10% was supported by broad-based growth across both credit and debit spending, with ecommerce continuing to grow faster than face-to-face spend.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in MD&A. The event-linked caveat is also stated there.
competitive_position.claim: Value-added services are a growing second pillar. VAS revenue was $14.2 billion in fiscal 2026, against $10.9 billion and $8.8 billion in the two prior years.
quotes: Value-added services revenue in fiscal 2026 increased 31% over the prior year, reflecting growth across all portfolios, with the largest contributions from Issuing Solutions and Advisory and Other Services.

competitive_position.claim: Visa's technology position includes contactless and tokenization. Tap to Pay made up 84% of face-to-face transactions globally and 76% in the U.S. in September 2026, and over 60% of ecommerce transactions were tokenized.
quotes: Tap to Pay has become the default way Visa cardholders pay, comprising 84% and 76% of face-to-face transactions globally and in the United States, respectively, in September 2026.
As of September 30, 2026, over 60% of ecommerce transactions were tokenized.

competitive_position.basis: The company's strategy is stated in Item 1. The expected benefit is management's belief, not a result.
competitive_position.claim: Visa is investing in agentic commerce and stablecoins to extend its position, and says stablecoin-linked card issuance has grown to over 225 programs across more than 50 countries.
quotes: We believe agentic commerce will expand our addressable market and drive future growth.
stablecoin-linked card issuance has expanded to over 225 programs across more than 50 countries

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement and MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Cash generation funds heavy capital return and acquisitions. Operating cash flow was 23,728 (table in millions), against 20,451 of class A repurchases and 5,112 of dividends (both table in millions). Visa also agreed to buy BioCatch for $2.4 billion and bought Prisma and Newpay for $1.5 billion.
quotes: In August 2026, we entered into a definitive agreement to acquire BioCatch, a leading provider of behavioral-first, multi-signal fraud intelligence, for $2.4 billion in cash.
In February 2026, we acquired Prisma Medios de Pago S.A.U. (Prisma) and Newpay S.A.U. (Newpay) in Argentina for a total purchase consideration of $1.5 billion in cash.

competitive_position.basis: Figures are stated in the statements and MD&A. The comparison of the two growth rates is the analyst's reading of those printed percentages.
competitive_position.claim: Client incentives are a rising cost of keeping clients. They reached 18,317 (table in millions) in fiscal 2026 from 15,751, up 16%, a little faster than the 15% growth in net revenue. Visa says pricing and incentive pressure could moderate its growth.
quotes: Continued pressures on pricing, incentives, fee discounts and rebates could moderate our growth.
Client incentives increased in fiscal 2026 over the prior year primarily due to growth in payments volume.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the risk factors. The size of the concentration is in a note not included in the excerpt.
competitive_position.claim: Client concentration is a named threat. A significant portion of net revenue comes from the largest clients, which can generally issue non-Visa products and may leave on relatively short notice.
quotes: Because a significant portion of our net revenue is concentrated among our largest clients, the loss of business from any one of them could materially harm our business, results of operations and financial condition.

competitive_position.claim: Interchange and fee regulation is a named threat. U.S. debit interchange rules are being revisited and court decisions conflict, and the Credit Card Competition Act has been reintroduced. Visa says it does not receive interchange directly but that interchange affects its volume and revenue.
quotes: Recent conflicting federal court decisions on the validity of Regulation II's interchange fee standard have created additional uncertainty and could result in a significantly lower interchange cap for debit transactions.
Although we generally do not receive IRF revenue directly, IRFs are a key competitive factor that affects our overall payments volume and net revenue.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the statements and MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Interchange litigation continues to weigh on results. The litigation provision was 1,764 (table in millions) in fiscal 2026 against 2,562 a year earlier. Estimated interchange at issue in unresolved U.S. covered claims was approximately $17.4 billion on May 11, 2026 and approximately $15.9 billion on October 1, 2026.
quotes: Litigation provision decreased in fiscal 2026 over the prior year primarily due to lower accruals related to the U.S. covered litigation.

The estimated interchange reimbursement fees at issue in unresolved claims for damages in the U.S. covered litigation was approximately $17.4 billion(1) as of May 11, 2026 and was approximately $15.9 billion(1) as of October 1, 2026.

competitive_position.claim: Sovereign and domestic payment systems are a named threat to market access. Governments seek to cut reliance on international networks, UnionPay remains predominant in China, and Visa needs further approval before it can start domestic clearing there.
quotes: Governments in numerous jurisdictions seek to strengthen domestic control over payments infrastructure and reduce reliance on international payment providers like Visa, through market access barriers, preferential domestic regulations, localization requirements and support for domestic systems.
In China, UnionPay remains the predominant domestic processor and acceptance network for bank cards.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the risk factors. How far these threats have already affected results is not shown.
competitive_position.claim: Intense competition and alternative payment systems are named threats. They include closed-loop rivals, real-time payment networks, digital wallets, stablecoins and AI-driven competitors. Visa warns these could reduce its role or bypass its network.
quotes: The global payments industry is intensely competitive and rapidly evolving.

We and our competitors are developing or participating in alternative payment systems, including mobile payments, P2P services, RTP initiatives, ACH/direct debit solutions and cryptocurrency-based platforms, including stablecoin payments, that could reduce our role or disintermediate us from transaction processing.

financial_health.basis: stated in the balance sheet; the interpretation of offsetting items is inferred from the line items
financial_health.claim: Cash and cash equivalents were 12,938 (table in millions) at fiscal year-end, down from 17,164 a year earlier. Total current assets were 30,486 against total current liabilities of 31,588, so current liabilities are slightly larger than current assets.
Cash, cash equivalents and investment securities totalled $14.2 billion at fiscal year-end, a measure the company itself reports.
quotes: Cash, cash equivalents and investment securities were $14.2 billion at September 30, 2026.

financial_health.basis: stated in the balance sheet and income statement; the coverage reading is inferred from those figures
financial_health.claim: Debt was 19,355 (table in millions) long-term plus 2,716 current maturities. Total liabilities were 58,249 against total equity of 36,111. Interest expense was 758 against operating income of 28,110.

financial_health.basis: stated in the cash flow statement; the conversion reading is inferred
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow was 23,728 (table in millions) in the latest year, up from 23,059 and 19,950 in the two prior years. That is close to net income of 23,504. Purchases of property, equipment and technology were 1,671.

financial_health.basis: stated in the cash flow lines; the mechanism is inferred
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow was affected by litigation and settlement timing. Accrued litigation was a use of cash of (2,040), after a source of 1,303 the year before. The settlement receivable was a source of 2,115 and the settlement payable a use of (1,833).

financial_health.basis: stated in the cash flow footnote; the comparison with the provision is inferred
financial_health.claim: Cash taxes paid were 5,684 (table in millions), above the prior year's 4,541 and above the income tax provision of 4,589. The filing footnote says the amount includes clean energy tax credit payments.
quotes: For each of fiscal 2026 and 2025, the amount includes cash paid for clean energy tax credits of $1.9 billion.

financial_health.basis: stated in the cash flow statement and MD&A
financial_health.claim: Shareholder returns used more cash than operations produced. Financing outflow was (28,241) (table in millions), including (20,451) of class A share repurchases and (5,112) of dividends. Cash, cash equivalents and restricted amounts fell by (5,869) to 19,118.
quotes: During fiscal 2026, we repurchased 61 million shares of our class A common stock in the open market for $20.5 billion.

financial_health.basis: stated in the balance sheet, cash flow statement and MD&A; the funding path is inferred
financial_health.claim: Debt falling due within one year was 2,716 (table in millions), down from 5,569 a year earlier. In the latest year the company repaid 5,565 of senior notes and issued 2,995, using new borrowing to meet part of the maturities.
quotes: In February 2026, we issued fixed-rate senior notes in a public offering in an aggregate principal amount of $3.0 billion, with maturities ranging between 3 and 10 years.

financial_health.basis: stated in MD&A, the 8-K and the balance sheet
financial_health.claim: Litigation funding is a further call on cash. The company recorded $1.6 billion of interchange litigation accruals and made $1.3 billion of escrow deposits in the latest year. A further $405 million deposit was authorized in September. Accrued litigation was 990 (table in millions), and the escrow cash balance was 628.
quotes: The additional accruals related to the interchange multidistrict litigation could be higher or lower than deposits made into the U.S. litigation escrow account.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the MD&A; the continuation condition is stated in the same passage.
growth_thesis.claim: Payments volume growth is a core driver. Nominal payments volume grew 10%, across both credit and debit, and ecommerce grew faster than face-to-face spend. It feeds service revenue of $19,918 (table in millions), up 14%. For this to continue, consumer spending must stay resilient and the shift to digital payments must keep adding volume.
quotes: Nominal payments volume growth of 10% was supported by broad-based growth across both credit and debit spending, with ecommerce continuing to grow faster than face-to-face spend.
Service revenue in a given quarter is primarily assessed based on nominal payments volume in the prior quarter.

growth_thesis.claim: Cross-border activity is a driver. Nominal cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe grew 15%, supported by cross-border ecommerce and travel. International transaction revenue was $15,251 (table in millions), up 8%. It continues only if cross-border ecommerce and travel keep growing and currency volatility does not fall further.
quotes: Cross-border volume growth was supported by cross-border ecommerce and travel-related activity.

International transaction revenue increased in fiscal 2026 over the prior year primarily due to growth in nominal cross-border volume of 15%, excluding transactions within Europe, partially offset by lower volatility of a broad range of currencies and business mix.

growth_thesis.claim: Processed transactions are a driver. They grew 9% to 281,331 (table in millions), and data processing revenue rose 17% to $23,374 (table in millions). For this to continue, transaction counts must keep growing and the pricing modifications, value-added services and cross-border mix that also lifted this line must persist.
quotes: Data processing revenue increased in fiscal 2026 over the prior year primarily due to growth in processed transactions of 9%, select pricing modifications, growth in value-added services and higher cross-border transaction mix.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the MD&A; the event-dependence is inferred from the cited marketing-demand sentence.
growth_thesis.claim: Value-added services are a fast-growing driver. Revenue was $14.2 billion against $10.9 billion the year before, up 31%. Client consulting engagements rose approximately 30%. For this to continue, client demand for consulting and issuing solutions must hold, and marketing-services demand must not fall back after the sponsorship events that lifted it.
quotes: Value-added services revenue in fiscal 2026 increased 31% over the prior year, reflecting growth across all portfolios, with the largest contributions from Issuing Solutions and Advisory and Other Services.
Demand for marketing services increased over the prior year primarily due to sponsorship events, including the FIFA World Cup 2026TM and the Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games Milano Cortina 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Pricing is named as a driver in the MD&A; the size of its contribution is not stated, and the condition is inferred from the risk factor.
growth_thesis.claim: Pricing modifications add to revenue growth in service, data processing and other revenue. Their continuation depends on clients accepting price changes despite competitive pressure on fees.
quotes: Other revenue increased in fiscal 2026 over the prior year primarily due to growth in Advisory and Other Services and select pricing modifications.
We also face intense competitive pressure on the prices we charge our financial institution clients.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the MD&A and risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Client incentives are the main offset to revenue growth. They were $18,317 (table in millions), up 16%, and they track payments volume. Net revenue growth can continue only if incentive growth stays manageable alongside volume growth.
quotes: Client incentives increased in fiscal 2026 over the prior year primarily due to growth in payments volume.
Continued pressures on pricing, incentives, fee discounts and rebates could moderate our growth.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release and MD&A.
growth_thesis.claim: Revenue growth was helped slightly by currency: net revenue rose 15%, or 14% on a constant-dollar basis. That part of growth depends on exchange rates and is not controlled by the company.
quotes: Net revenue of $45.9B, an increase of 15%, or 14% on a constant-dollar basis
Foreign exchange rate movements and volatility have contributed to periodic variability in our results, and may continue to do so in the future.

growth_thesis.basis: Buyback and share-count figures are stated; the link to EPS growth is inferred from the statements.
growth_thesis.claim: Earnings per share grew faster than net income, helped by buybacks. The company repurchased 61 million class A shares for $20.5 billion, with $24.4 billion of authorization remaining. Diluted weighted-average class A shares were 1,907 against 1,966 a year earlier. Operating cash flow of 23,728 (table in millions) funded this. Continuing it requires sustained cash generation.
quotes: During fiscal 2026, we repurchased 61 million shares of our class A common stock in the open market for $20.5 billion.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the MD&A; the comparison with revenue growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Cost growth must stay near revenue growth for earnings to keep rising. GAAP operating expenses rose 11%, driven by personnel and marketing. Non-GAAP operating expenses rose 16%, slightly above the 15% revenue growth.
quotes: Operating expenses increased 11% over the prior year, primarily driven by higher personnel and marketing expenses.
Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 16% over the prior year, primarily driven by higher personnel, marketing and professional fees.

growth_thesis.basis: Provision figures and growth rates are stated; the reading that it widened the gap between GAAP and non-GAAP growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: A lower litigation provision lifted GAAP net income growth (17%) above non-GAAP net income growth (12%). The provision was 1,764 (table in millions) against 2,562 the year before. This is not a repeatable growth source because it depends on future litigation accruals.
quotes: Litigation provision decreased in fiscal 2026 over the prior year primarily due to lower accruals related to the U.S. covered litigation.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated as management belief in Item 1; the conditions come from Item 1A.
growth_thesis.claim: Management names agentic commerce and stablecoins as future growth areas, but the evidence gives no revenue figures for either. They depend on ecosystem adoption and on unsettled legal frameworks.
quotes: We believe agentic commerce will expand our addressable market and drive future growth.

Legal frameworks governing autonomous agents remain nascent, and the interplay between payments regulations, data privacy laws and evolving AI rules creates uncertainty around compliance obligations and liability exposure.

growth_thesis.basis: Deal terms are stated; any growth effect is inferred and not quantified.
growth_thesis.claim: Acquisitions add capability and some expense, but their revenue contribution is not quantified. Argentine acquisitions were completed for $1.5 billion in cash. A $2.4 billion BioCatch acquisition is pending and subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals.
quotes: This acquisition is subject to customary closing conditions, including applicable regulatory approvals.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the risk factors; the effect on growth is not quantified.
growth_thesis.claim: Regulation of interchange is a condition that could limit growth. Visa generally does not receive interchange directly, but interchange affects volume and net revenue. A possible lower U.S. debit cap and other jurisdictions' caps would change the economics of Visa's network.
quotes: Although we generally do not receive IRF revenue directly, IRFs are a key competitive factor that affects our overall payments volume and net revenue.

Recent conflicting federal court decisions on the validity of Regulation II's interchange fee standard have created additional uncertainty and could result in a significantly lower interchange cap for debit transactions.

material_events.claim: Visa signed a definitive agreement to acquire BioCatch for $2.4 billion in cash. The deal is subject to closing conditions, including regulatory approvals.
quotes: In August 2026, we entered into a definitive agreement to acquire BioCatch, a leading provider of behavioral-first, multi-signal fraud intelligence, for $2.4 billion in cash.

material_events.claim: Visa acquired Prisma and Newpay in Argentina for total cash consideration of $1.5 billion.
quotes: In February 2026, we acquired Prisma Medios de Pago S.A.U. (Prisma) and Newpay S.A.U. (Newpay) in Argentina for a total purchase consideration of $1.5 billion in cash.

material_events.claim: Visa accepted tendered class B-1 and B-2 common shares in an exchange offer and retired them. In return it issued class B-3 and class C common stock.
quotes: In May 2026, we accepted 3 million shares of class B-1 common stock and 120 million shares of class B-2 common stock tendered in the exchange offer.

material_events.claim: Visa issued fixed-rate senior notes in a public offering with an aggregate principal amount of $3.0 billion.
quotes: In February 2026, we issued fixed-rate senior notes in a public offering in an aggregate principal amount of $3.0 billion, with maturities ranging between 3 and 10 years.

material_events.claim: Visa's board authorized an additional $20.0 billion share repurchase program.
quotes: In April 2026, our board of directors authorized an additional $20.0 billion share repurchase program, providing multi-year flexibility.

material_events.claim: Visa recorded additional interchange multidistrict litigation accruals of $1.6 billion and made additional U.S. litigation escrow deposits of $1.3 billion.
quotes: During fiscal 2026, we recorded additional accruals of $1.6 billion to address claims associated with the interchange multidistrict litigation.
We also made additional deposits of $1.3 billion into the U.S. litigation escrow account.

material_events.claim: Visa authorized a $405 million deposit into the U.S. litigation escrow account. This lowered the conversion rates of its class B-1, B-2 and B-3 common stock.
quotes: On September 18, 2026, Visa Inc. (the “Company”) authorized the deposit of $405 million into the U.S. litigation escrow account previously established under the Company’s U.S. retrospective responsibility plan (the “Plan”).

material_events.claim: Visa's board raised the quarterly cash dividend 16% to $0.780 per share. It is payable on December 1, 2026 to holders of record as of November 10, 2026.
quotes: The board of directors increased Visa's quarterly cash dividend 16% to $0.780 per share

material_events.claim: The People's Bank of China approved Visa's Application to Prepare for a domestic bank card clearing institution. Further regulatory approval is still needed before clearing operations can begin.
quotes: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) accepted our application to operate a Bank Card Clearing Institution (BCCI) in June 2020, and approved our Application to Prepare in October 2026, which permits us to begin formal preparations to establish a domestic BCCI.

quotes: The failure of one or both of the retrospective responsibility plans to adequately insulate us from the impact of such settlements, judgments, losses or liabilities could materially harm our financial condition or cash flows, or even cause us to become insolvent.
